clue.text: I love Latin school book

parts.note: amo is the Latin for 'I love', the first verb form every Latin pupil learns

explanation.surface: A pupil declares a fondness for their Latin textbook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Latin school book' reads as one thing, but 'Latin' belongs with 'I love', telling you to translate it.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: this is one of the prophetic books of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Take a short time to promote last of waitrose's wine

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a short time
to sell an idea is to promote it

indicators.note: last of asks for the final letter of the shop's name, ignoring the possessive

explanation.surface: Someone is told to spend a few minutes pushing the supermarket's remaining bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last of' takes the final E of waitrose; the possessive 's just links to the definition. Waitrose is a British supermarket chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a white variety from the river valley shared by France and Germany.

clue.text: Warm European country — but not in spring

indicators.note: but not says the following word's letters are to be left off the country

parts.note: Spain is a European country with a warm climate
taken as written

explanation.surface: A European country is warm for most of the year except the months after winter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not' removes IN from SPAIN. 'Spring' wants to be the season; it is a source of mineral water.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a mineral water source where people go for health cures.

clue.text: Cotton, sage and straw?

parts.note: a sage is a wise person, as is a seer
a drinking straw is whimsically a thing you suck through, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A list of three plant products: a fibre, a herb and dried stalks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sage' looks like the herb but is the wise man; the question mark excuses the fanciful description of a drinking straw.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a puckered, striped fabric usually woven from this fibre.

clue.text: They are a key part of ship!

definitions.text: They are a key part of ship!

indicators.note: part of says the keyboard key sits within the letters for the vessel

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
Alt is a key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: Some people or things are an essential component of a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: 'part of' is the insertion indicator, and old seamen really are vital to a crew.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang term for experienced sailors, who are essential members of a vessel's crew.

clue.text: Ape drops dead bird

indicators.note: drops says the word for ape lets go of the letters that follow

parts.note: to ape someone is to emulate or copy them
late means dead, as in 'the late Mr Smith'

explanation.surface: A monkey lets a lifeless feathered creature fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops' removes LATE from EMULATE. 'Ape' is a verb here, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a large flightless Australian species.

clue.text: Covered tracks to protect a senior civil servant

parts.note: something covered is hidden or secret
Ry is the abbreviation for railway, which is tracks

explanation.surface: Someone hid the evidence to shield a high-ranking official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to protect' puts A inside RY. 'Covered tracks' reads as one phrase but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the top official of a government department is a Permanent one of these.

clue.text: Slob out with top coach jogging

indicators.note: jogging means shaking or nudging, so the letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone lazes about while an elite trainer goes for a run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slob out' reads as a verb phrase, but 'Slob' alone is the definition and 'out' is part of the fodder that 'jogging' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for a lazy person who lounges watching television all day.

clue.text: Swimmer's toupee bobbing round end of pool

definitions.note: the possessive is read as 'swimmer is', leaving a noun as definition

indicators.note: round says the rearranged hairpiece letters go around the letter picked from pool
bobbing means moving up and down, so the letters shift about
end of asks for the final letter of pool

explanation.surface: A bather's hairpiece floats about at the far side of the baths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bobbing' rearranges TOUPEE to EEPOUT, and 'round' puts it about the L from 'end of' pool. A 'swimmer' is the crossword way of saying fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an elongated fish, which crosswords fancifully call a swimmer.

clue.text: Criticize excellent learner after dunce

indicators.note: after says the excellent learner pieces follow the word for dunce

parts.note: an ass is a fool or dunce
A1, written AI, means first-class or excellent
L is the abbreviation for learner, as on a driver's L-plate

explanation.surface: A teacher is told to rebuke the star pupil once the class fool has been dealt with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' orders the pieces: dunce first, then excellent and learner. L-plates are shown on a learner driver's car in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to attack verbally.

clue.text: Left a Parisian dessert outside to separate

parts.note: un is the French for 'a', as someone from Paris would say it

indicators.note: outside says the French article and the pudding together go around the letter for left

parts.note: a coupe is an ice-cream dessert served in a glass dish

explanation.surface: Someone put a Frenchman's pudding outdoors so it would split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps UN COUPE around L. 'Left' looks like a verb but is just the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to disconnect, as with railway carriages.

clue.text: Narrow escape resulting in barefaced cheek?

definitions.meaning: a near miss, a lucky avoidance of disaster
a thorough going-over with a razor leaves the side of the face smooth and bare

explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for a near miss, and literally a razor job that leaves the face smooth.

clue.text: Camper's provision for retirement

parts.note: retirement here is going to bed, not stopping work, so this is what someone under canvas has ready for the night

explanation.definitionFit: Retiring means going to bed, and this is what someone in a tent beds down in.

clue.text: Worm girl found on hat

indicators.note: found on says, in a down clue, the name sits on top of the hat

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name
lid is slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A wriggly creature is discovered on a young lady's headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the segmented group that includes earthworms and leeches.

clue.text: Pan's enemy shot on the side of leg

definitions.meaning: the pirate captain who is Peter Pan's foe in J M Barrie's story

definitions.text: shot on the side of leg
definitions.meaning: a cricket stroke that sends a short ball round to the leg side, the half of the field behind the batter's legs

explanation.definitionFit: Barrie's pirate captain and a cricket stroke played to the leg side share this name.

clue.text: Set on showing this charity event

definitions.text: Set on showing this charity event

parts.words: Set on showing this charity event
parts.note: the set is a television set: when it is switched on it may be showing this long fundraising broadcast

explanation.definitionFit: A long fundraising broadcast is what a switched-on television would be displaying.

clue.text: Small boy stands on a border — such might get you madder!

indicators.note: stands on says, in a down clue, the short name is placed above the rest

parts.note: Herb is the short form of the boy's name Herbert
a list is a border or selvage of cloth

explanation.surface: A little lad balances on an edge, and that sort of thing could make you angrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'madder' looks like 'more angry' but is the plant whose root gives a red dye, something a plant specialist could supply.
explanation.definitionFit: A dealer in medicinal plants could supply the dye plant in question.

clue.text: Rodent — American one carrying disease of the joints

indicators.note: carrying says the two single letters hold the ailment between them

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
gout is a painful inflammation of the joints

explanation.surface: A rat from the United States is infected with something like arthritis.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a long-legged species from Central and South America.

clue.text: Proust novel inducing lethargy

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new, so the writer's name takes a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A very long French book sends its reader into a doze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like the book Proust wrote but is the anagram indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a dazed, sluggish state.

clue.text: Short film plugging caravan

definitions.meaning: a brief clip of footage that advertises a forthcoming film
a towed vehicle; Americans use this word for what the British call a caravan

explanation.definitionFit: A brief advert for a coming film and a towed holiday home are both called this.

clue.text: Ruin ballad with a rotten set

parts.note: a lay is a narrative poem or song, a ballad

indicators.note: rotten means gone bad, so the letters of the word beside it are disturbed

explanation.surface: A band spoils a song by playing it in a dreadful concert performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rotten' rearranges SET to STE. 'with' is not a link here: it supplies W.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to devastate or destroy utterly.

clue.text: Kitsch container on German lace

indicators.note: on says, in a down clue, the first pieces sit above the letter for German

parts.note: tat is British slang for tasteless, shoddy goods
a tin is a metal container

explanation.surface: A tasteless pot sits on a piece of delicate German needlework.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a knotted kind made with a small shuttle.

clue.text: Try to please supporter when out of work

indicators.note: out of is read as outside of, so the supporter goes around the letter for work

parts.note: a fan is a supporter of a team or star
W is the physics symbol for work

explanation.surface: A loyal follower who has lost a job does everything to win favour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' means outside, wrapping FAN around W. 'out of work' reads as unemployed.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to seek favour by flattering and grovelling.

clue.text: Sort of hand shuffled etc

indicators.note: shuffled, as with a pack of cards, mixes the letters of the first three words

explanation.surface: A card player describes the kind of cards dealt after mixing the pack, and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shuffled' rearranges SORT OF HAND; the abbreviation at the close, easy to skip as filler, is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The English phrase that the Latin abbreviation stands for.

clue.text: Dirty topless drunk …

indicators.note: topless says, in a down clue, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: soiled means dirty or stained

explanation.surface: A grubby reveller with no shirt on is intoxicated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes the S that begins SOILED. The ellipsis only joins the surface to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym, usually heard as 'well' so.

clue.text: Gathering going out on a Saturday night?

definitions.meaning: joining together, as people do when pooling money for a shared purchase

definitions.text: going out on a Saturday night?
definitions.meaning: spending the evening dancing at nightspots, a typical weekend outing

explanation.definitionFit: Banding together to pool resources and a night out dancing share this word.

clue.text: … Girl wants a strong tipple

indicators.note: wants in its old sense of lacks, so the name goes without the letter that follows

parts.note: Gina is a girl's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young woman would like a stiff drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wants' means lacks, removing A from GINA. The ellipsis merely continues the previous clue's boozy scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a juniper-flavoured spirit.

clue.text: One introduces trendy star at opening

indicators.note: at opening says the word for star goes at the front, before the word for trendy

parts.note: the star of a film or play is its lead
in means fashionable or trendy

explanation.surface: A compere presents a fashionable celebrity at a first night.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage or remark that introduces what follows.

clue.text: Contributor to Cleopatra's poisoning

indicators.note: a contributor to the phrase is a run of letters that forms part of it

explanation.surface: Something played a part in the Egyptian queen's death by venom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contributor to' marks a run of letters spanning the two words after it, and the whole clue describes the snake said to have killed the queen.
explanation.definitionFit: By tradition the Egyptian queen died from the bite of this snake.

clue.text: Being scared after fellow was corrected

indicators.note: after says the corrected piece follows the letter for fellow

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS
to righten is to set right, so was corrected is rightened

explanation.surface: Someone is alarmed once a chap has been put straight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts RIGHTENED behind F. Righten is a rare verb meaning to put right.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: in a state of fear.

clue.text: Call out the name of lad wanted to run errands

definitions.meaning: to summon someone over a public address system
a boy employed in a hotel or court to carry messages

explanation.definitionFit: Summoning someone over a loudspeaker and a messenger boy share this word.
